bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to employment; paid leave; allowing an employee to opt out of participation in the paid leave program; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 268B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+[268B.101] EMPLOYEE OPT-OUT. +]

[+An employee may opt out of participation in the family or medical benefit program under this chapter by submitting a form to the commissioner electing to opt out of participation. The commissioner must create and make available in hard copy and online a form for employees subject to this chapter to use in opting out of participation in either the family or medical benefit program, or both programs. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective the day following final enactment. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to employment; paid leave; allowing an employee to opt out of participation in the paid leave program; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 268B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[268B.101] EMPLOYEE OPT-OUT.

An employee may opt out of participation in the family or medical benefit program under this chapter by submitting a form to the commissioner electing to opt out of participation. The commissioner must create and make available in hard copy and online a form for employees subject to this chapter to use in opting out of participation in either the family or medical benefit program, or both programs.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.
additions: An employee may opt out of participation in the family or medical benefit program under this chapter by submitting a form to the commissioner electing to opt out of participation. The commissioner must create and make available in hard copy and online a form for employees subject to this chapter to use in opting out of participation in either the family or medical benefit program, or both programs.
This section is effective the day following final enactment.
